extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and supervisory patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners on performing searches, handling applicant submissions (including replies to 37 CFR 1.105 and IDS-type filings), use of Patentability Reports, and making rejections under 35 U.S.C. and 37 C.F.R. standards during examination and prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of areas of search
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of areas of search must be considered and the examiner must indicate which areas were used and which areas were not used in performing a search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indication may be placed in the file wrapper search notes or made by notations on the applicant's reply with the examiner's initials and date; for Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, see IFW Manual section 3.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of answers to queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Information constituting answers to queries posed by the examiner or another Office employee must be considered, and the record must indicate that the answers were considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A minimal indication may be 'Considered' with the initials and date of the person making such consideration; see IFW Manual section 3.7 for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art submitted in response to 37 CFR 1.105 must be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Art that is submitted in response to a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement must be considered, at least to the extent art submitted with an Information Disclosure Statement under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 is considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant provides a written list of citations with a reply to a 1.105 requirement, examiner must indicate on that list which art has been considered and which has not, in the same manner as with an IDS (37 CFR 1.97/1.98). If applicant provides no list, examiner is not required to prepare one or otherwise make the submitted art of record unless the examiner relies on such art in a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 37 CFR 1.105 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Information beyond the scope of a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement, submitted along with information responding to a requirement under 37 CFR 1.105, need not be considered unless the submission of such art conforms to the provisions of 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 and MPEP § 609.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criteria for measuring the scope of a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement is the plain meaning of the text of the requirement; it is essential that the scope of information required be carefully specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.181 not a reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants seeking withdrawal or modification of a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement, or seeking to have information submitted under 1.105 considered, may submit a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to the Director of the Technology Center in which the requirement was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 1.181 is not a reply to a 1.105 requirement; the time period for the applicant to reply to the 1.105 requirement continues to run even where a petition has been submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial reply time exception to 37 CFR 1.97/1.98
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial reply, if responsive to the requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 and submitted within the original time period for reply (including any extensions), does not have to satisfy the fee and/or certification requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should list the references on a copy of Form PTO-1449 or PTO/SB/08 to have the citations entered in the record; any replies made subsequent to the initial reply must meet the provisions of 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Office action limitation after 1.105 reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Where information is submitted in a reply to a requirement under 37 CFR 1.105, the examiner may NOT make the next Office action relying on that art final unless all instances of the application of such art are necessitated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice is explicitly distinguished from practice following submission of an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97/1.98 (see MPEP § 609.04(b) and § 706.07(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Patentability Reports (P.R.) only in extraordinary circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application contains one or more claims classifiable in one or more other Technology Centers (TCs) which are not divisible inter se from the claims governing classification in the first TC, the application may be referred to the other TC(s) for a Patentability Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentability Report practice is only to be used in extraordinary circumstances and should be resorted to only where it will save total examiner time or result in improved quality due to specialized knowledge (see MPEP § 705.01(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability Report memorandum content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patentability Report is in memorandum form and will include the citation of all pertinent references and a complete action on all claims involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The field of search covered should be endorsed on the file wrapper by the examiner making the report; when signed by the primary examiner in the reporting TC, the P.R. will be returned to the TC to which the application is regularly assigned and placed in the file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction between primary examiners on P.R. disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the primary examiner in the TC having jurisdiction does not agree with the Patentability Report or any portion thereof, he or she may consult with the primary examiner responsible for the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agreement cannot be reached, the primary examiner having jurisdiction need not rely on the P.R. but may make his or her own action on the referred claims, in which case the P.R. should be removed from the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on when P.R. practice is proper
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability Report practice is not proper where claims are directed to the same character of invention but differ in scope only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemplary situations where P.R.s are ordinarily not proper include: (A) claims related as a manufacturing process and a product defined by the process; (B) claims related as product and a process which merely involves the fact that a product having certain characteristics is made; (C) claims related as a combination distinguished solely by characteristics of a subcombination and such subcombination per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval required for Patentability Report use
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it can be shown that a Patentability Report will save total examiner time, one is permitted with the approval of the Director of the Technology Center to which the application is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Approved' stamp should be impressed on the memorandum requesting the Patentability Report; see IFW Manual for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner preparing P.R. entitled to explanatory assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner preparing the Patentability Report will be entitled to receive an explanation of the disclosure from the examiner to whom the case is assigned to avoid duplication of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps reduce duplication and improves efficiency of the P.R. practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of examination in P.R. cases
rubrics_metrics.description: If supervisory patent examiners concerned in a P.R. case cannot agree as to the order of examination by their TCs, the supervisory patent examiner having jurisdiction of the application will direct that a complete search be made of the art relevant to his or her claims prior to referring the application to another TC for report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TC to which the application is referred will be advised of the results of this search; if supervisors think a different sequence is expedient, the order of search should be modified accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting and recording Patentability Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The forwarding of the application for a Patentability Report is not to be treated as a transfer by the forwarding TC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the P.R. is completed and application returned, it is not counted as a receipt or action by transfer; credit is given for time spent. Date status is determined based on dates in the TC of original jurisdiction; timely reminders should be furnished to the reporting TC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate prints of drawings for P.R. cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In P.R. applications having drawings, the examiner to whom the case is assigned will furnish to the TC to which the application is referred prints of such sheets of the drawings as are applicable, for interference search purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate by pencil notation on the file wrapper that duplicate prints have been furnished; see IFW Manual section 3.1 for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification on allowance/abandonment to reporting TCs
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application that has had P.R. prosecution is passed for issue or becomes abandoned, notification of this fact will at once be given by the TC having jurisdiction to each TC that submitted a Patentability Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner of each reporting TC will note the date of allowance or abandonment on the duplicate set of prints; when prints become of no value they may be destroyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews in P.R. cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In situations where an interview is held on an application in which a Patentability Report has been adopted, the reporting Technology Center may be called on for assistance at the interview when it concerns claims treated by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 713 to § 713.10 regarding interviews in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and goal of rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: After the application has been read and the claimed invention understood, a prior art search is made and the application reviewed to determine whether the claims define a useful, novel, nonobvious, and enabled invention that has been clearly described in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal of examination is to clearly articulate any rejection early so applicant can provide evidence of patentability; examiner then reviews all evidence, including arguments and evidence responsive to any rejection, before issuing the next Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 37 CFR 1.105 for information reasonably necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner determines that information reasonably necessary for the examination should be required from the applicant under 37 CFR 1.105, such a requirement should generally be made either prior to or with the first Office action on the merits and should follow procedures in MPEP § 704.10 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 1.105 requirements to obtain necessary factual information during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's duty to allow proper claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the manual explains the procedure in rejecting claims, the examiner should never overlook the importance of his or her role in allowing claims which properly define the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be constructive and aim to allow claims that meet statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.104(c)(2) citation of best references
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a reference is complex or shows inventions other than that claimed, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable; the pertinence of each reference, if not apparent, must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on admissions and examiner knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant, or the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding, as to any matter affecting patentability and may also rely upon facts within his or her knowledge pursuant to paragraph (d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document any reliance on admissions or on facts within examiner knowledge as part of the rejection rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform application of patentability standards and burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards of patentability applied in the examination of claims must be the same throughout the Office; all requirements for patentability (e.g., novelty, usefulness and unobviousness under 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103) must be met before a claim is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard applied is the 'preponderance of the evidence' test—reject a claim if, in view of prior art and evidence of record, it is more likely than not that the claim is unpatentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling defects in form or omission of a limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application discloses patentable subject matter but the claims in their present form cannot be allowed because of defects in form or omission of a limitation, the examiner should not stop with a bare objection or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's action should be constructive and, when possible, offer a definite suggestion for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noting patentable subject matter disclosed but not claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner is satisfied after the search that patentable subject matter has been disclosed and the record indicates applicant intends to claim such subject matter, the examiner may note in the Office action that certain aspects or features have not been claimed and that if properly claimed such claims may be given favorable consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Office action to advise applicant of potentially allowable unclaimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration after reply (37 CFR 1.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: After reply by applicant to a non-final action, the application will be reconsidered and again examined; applicant will be notified if claims are rejected, objections or requirements made, or decisions favorable to patentability are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may reply to such Office action in the same manner provided in 37 CFR 1.111 (or applicable provisions) unless the Office action is made final or appeal taken; see 37 CFR 1.116 and related rules for amendments post-appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between rejections and objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal to grant claims because the subject matter as claimed is considered unpatentable is called a 'rejection'; if the form of the claim is improper, an 'objection' is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rejection (merits) is subject to review by the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences; an objection (formal) if persisted may be reviewed only by petition to the Director. Do not combine formal matters with appeals to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of prior art: best available and avoid cumulative rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art rejections should ordinarily be confined strictly to the best available art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be made (e.g., when propriety depends on particular claim interpretation, when a reference meets a claim only in terms, or when a reference seems likely to be antedated by a §1.131 affidavit/declaration). Avoid merely cumulative rejections which would fall if the primary rejection is not sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance upon abstracts and foreign language documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When an abstract is used to support a rejection, the evidence relied upon is the facts contained in the abstract, not additional facts that may be contained in the underlying full text document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine whether both abstract and the underlying document are prior art, obtain and analyze the full text; if the document is not in English, obtain a translation. If relying on an abstract alone in a non-final OA, supply the full text (and translation if necessary) in the next Office action; whether the next action may be made final is governed by MPEP § 706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation) and 103 (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102, the reference must teach every aspect of the claimed invention explicitly or implicitly; for a 103 rejection, the reference teachings must be modified to meet the claims, and the modification must have been obvious to one of ordinary skill at the time the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MPEP § 2131 - § 2146 for guidance on patentability determinations under 102 and 103; be clear in language of rejection (see MPEP § 707.07(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining the effective filing date (continuation/divisional/CIP rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective filing date may be the same as an earlier application where requirements of 35 U.S.C. 120 and 365(c) are satisfied; for continuation-in-part (CIP), claims not supported by parent have effective filing date equal to new application, whereas claims fully supported by the earlier parent have the parent's effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine support under 35 U.S.C. 112 and applicable statutes to ascertain effective filing dates for claims.
